title: Differential order detects open immersions of smooth trait models
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $E$, residue field $k$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. Smooth and finite type have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for a strict henselization at a geometric closed point and $E^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. An open in a scheme over a trait is base-dense if it is dense in each fibre. A rational map over that trait is a morphism on a base-dense open, modulo agreement on a base-dense common open; its domain of definition is the union of all representative domains. A birational map over the trait is an isomorphism between base-dense opens. For a smooth separated finite-type $E$-scheme $X$, a smooth model means a smooth separated finite-type $T$-scheme $M$ with a specified identification $M_E\simeq X$. Let $G/E$ be a smooth separated finite-type group scheme of dimension $d$, with group operations as in [def-sc-group-scheme]. Fix a nowhere vanishing left-invariant section $\omega$ of $\Omega^d_{G/E}=\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{G/E}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. For a smooth model $M$ of $G$ with nonempty irreducible special fibre and generic point $\zeta$ of that fibre, write $n(M)=\operatorname{ord}_{\zeta}(\omega)$: this is the integer $n$ for which $\pi^{-n}\omega$ generates $\Omega^d_{M/R,\zeta}$. Each ring $\mathcal O_{M,\zeta}$ used to define $n(M)$ is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, so the indicated integer exists uniquely. Every smooth model with nonempty special fibre admits an $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-point. Let $M,N$ have nonempty irreducible special fibres and let $u:M\dashrightarrow N$ be a $T$-rational map whose generic fibre is an isomorphism $u_E:G\to G$. Write $u_E^*\omega=a\omega$ for a unit $a\in\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)^\times$. If $v(a(x))=0$ for an $E^{\mathrm{sh}}$-point $x$ extending to $M(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$, then $n(M)\geq n(N)$, and the morphism on the domain of definition of $u$ is an open immersion if and only if $n(M)=n(N)$. More generally, the open-immersion assertion holds for models with finitely many special-fibre components if every source and target component has the same differential order $n_0$, and for each source component the unit-multiplier hypothesis holds on the open consisting of that component and the entire generic fibre. In this last assertion the conclusion is an open immersion on the entire domain of definition, not merely near the generic points of special-fibre components.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-volume-infrastructure] to each model. The generic fibre is the smooth group $G$. By [lem-sfb-group-scheme-differentials-from-identity], $\Omega^1_{G/E}\cong f^*e^*\Omega^1_{G/E}$ is free of one constant rank $r$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] $r=\dim_xG$ at every $x\in G$; hence $G$ is pure of dimension $r=d$. So the differential sheaves of the models have rank $d$ and their determinants are line bundles. The special-fibre generic stalks are DVRs with uniformizer $\pi$. A nonzero vector in a free rank-one module over the fraction field of a DVR has a unique integral order (write its coefficient as $\pi^n$ times a unit). This defines $n(M)$ and $n(N)$ exactly as stated. Smoothness also makes special-fibre components pairwise disjoint, so deleting the other components gives an open consisting of a chosen component and the entire generic fibre.

source.place: 4.3 order construction, printed p.104; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Every smooth model $Z$ with nonempty special fibre has an $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-point. Its generic fibre is dense by [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-volume-infrastructure], hence nonempty; therefore $Z\to T$ is surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] in its scheme case to obtain a jointly surjective etale family $T_i\to T$ and maps $T_i\to Z$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], its base change to $\operatorname{Spec}R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is still a jointly surjective etale family of schemes. Choose a member with a point over the closed point. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] (with $Y=T$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_R$) the ring $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is canonically the colimit $C$ over the triples category with $K$ the separable closure of $k$ in $\Omega$; so $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is strictly henselian, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_RR^{\mathrm{sh}}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. Thus [lem-sbc-strict-henselian-etale-neighbourhood-section] gives a section of that member, hence a point of $Z(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] this ring is a DVR, and its maximal-ideal description says that $\pi$ is its uniformizer.

source.place: 2.2 Corollary 13 and Proposition 14; 2.3 Proposition 5; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Set $n_M=n(M)$ and $n_N=n(N)$. By [lem-sfb-trait-line-section-order-normalization], $\alpha_M=\pi^{-n_M}\omega$ and $\alpha_N=\pi^{-n_N}\omega$ extend to global frames of the respective top-differential lines. Apply the same node with $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_M$ and $s_E=a$. It writes $a=\pi^m c$ with $c$ a global unit of $M$, and identifies $m$ with the valuation at the section in the hypothesis. Hence $m=0$, so $a$ itself extends as a global unit on $M$.

source.place: 4.3 normalization paragraphs preceding Lemma 1; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $U$ be the domain of definition. It contains the entire generic fibre: glue the representative with the specified generic-fibre morphism, using the uniqueness for maps from a smooth trait scheme to a separated target in [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-local-rational-spreading]. It contains the generic point of the special fibre by base-density. On $U$ the determinant of the differential gives a regular coefficient $b$ with $u^*\alpha_N=b\alpha_M$. On the generic fibre the equation is $b=\pi^{n_M-n_N}a$. Since $a$ is a unit, at the special-fibre generic DVR the order of $b$ is $n_M-n_N$. A regular nonzero element of a DVR has nonnegative order; hence $n_M\geq n_N$.

source.place: 4.3 Lemma 1 proof, determinant equation; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: If $n_M=n_N$, the coefficient $b$ equals the unit $a$ on $U$: the equality holds on $U_E$, and generic-fibre restriction is injective by [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-volume-infrastructure]. Thus $\bigwedge^d du$ is an isomorphism everywhere on $U$, and [lem-sfb-smooth-cotangent-etale-criterion] makes $u$ etale everywhere there. It is separated because $U$ is separated over the trait (its relative diagonal over $N$ is the base change of its closed diagonal over the trait). Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-isomorphism-dense-open] in the scheme case with target $N$ and quasi-compact schematically dense open $N_E$: etale means flat and locally of finite presentation, hence locally finite type, and $U\times_NN_E=U_E\simeq N_E$. This proves an open immersion on all of $U$.

source.place: 4.3 Lemma 1(ii), using 2.2 Corollary 10 and the generic-isomorphism open-immersion criterion; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely, an open immersion identifies the relative differential sheaves by restriction, so its determinant is invertible. In particular $b$ is a unit at the source special-fibre generic point. Its order there is $n_M-n_N$ by step 4, and a DVR unit has order zero. Therefore $n_M=n_N$.

source.place: 4.3 Lemma 1(ii), reverse implication; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: For finitely many components of common order $n_0$, [lem-sfb-trait-line-section-order-normalization] gives global frames $\pi^{-n_0}\omega$ on both models. Write the determinant coefficient on the entire domain as $b$. For each source component $C$, restrict the generic unit $a$ to the open $M_C$ consisting of $C$ and $M_E$. The section hypothesis and the normalization node give order zero for $a$ on $C$, and in fact a unit extension on $M_C$. Since the exponents are both $n_0$, the equation is $b=a$ on the generic fibre, hence on $U\cap M_C$ by schematic density. These opens cover $U$ (or $U=U_E$ when the source special fibre is empty). Therefore $b$ is a unit throughout $U$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-cotangent-etale-criterion] and the same dense-open criterion [lem-sfb-space-flat-isomorphism-dense-open] as in step 5 to the whole morphism $U\to N$. This proves the asserted global open immersion without separately gluing componentwise images.
